Class MKTooltip

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.MKTooltip
public final class MKTooltip extends Object
The one place a hover tooltip is queued: every element tooltip and the panel tooltip go through queue(GuiGraphicsExtractor, Component, int, int) instead of calling vanilla's setTooltipForNextFrame directly.

Why it exists

Vanilla's hover tooltips have no maximum width, so a long one draws as a single line across the screen. The cap belongs in one default that every tooltip inherits, not in each element: how wide a tooltip may be is the same for every element, while when to show one varies (a button hides it while pressed, a dropdown chooses between the trigger's and a row's). Every tooltip site already made the same vanilla call, graphics.setTooltipForNextFrame(font, component, mx, my), so this class is a thin wrapper over that call.

Why a tooltip is capped when panels are not

Laid-out panel content grows to fit what it holds. A tooltip follows the mouse with no layout around it to bound it, so growing to fit is exactly what draws the line across the screen. The cap does for tooltips what the screen edge does for panels. It wraps with Font.split, the splitter TextLabel uses, so both wrap the same way.

This class also holds the switches a mod can turn on for every tooltip in the game: hideWhen(BooleanSupplier), wrapWhen(BooleanSupplier), clampWhen(BooleanSupplier), avoidCoverWhen(BooleanSupplier) and onWheel(MKTooltip.Wheel).

  • Field Details

    • MIN_WRAP_WIDTH

      public static final int MIN_WRAP_WIDTH
      The narrowest a tooltip's text is ever wrapped to on one side of the cursor, in GUI pixels: about ten characters of vanilla's font, two short words a line, below which a sentence reads one word at a time. A side with less room than this (or than the tooltip's longest word or image) is ruled out unless the tooltip already fits there.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • EDGE

      public static final int EDGE
      Gap kept between a scrolled tooltip and the screen edge, in GUI pixels (vanilla's own minimum).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH

      public static final int DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH
      The default maximum tooltip width, in GUI pixels: about seven average words. Seven words of about 5 characters plus a space is about 40 characters, and Minecraft's default font averages about 6 px per glyph (the 1 px gap included), so about 200 px. A wider tooltip wraps onto more lines. Values from about 180 to 220 work; widen it if seven words feels tight in game.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

      public static void hideWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Hides every tooltip in the game, on any screen and from any source (vanilla, MenuKit elements, other mods), on every frame condition is true. Several mods may register; any one returning true hides. Registering the same supplier instance twice is a no-op. Call from client init.

    • wrapWhen

      public static void wrapWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Wraps every tooltip to the screen's width on every frame condition is true: a text line wider than wrapWidth(int) breaks onto more lines (vanilla's splitter, breaking at spaces) and the tooltip is kept inside the screen's sides. Images (a bundle's grid, a map) are left as they are. A wrapped first line stays one title: the gap under it and the scroll pin take all of its lines. Several mods may register; any one returning true wraps. Call from client init.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze

    • clampWhen

      public static void clampWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Keeps every tooltip's top at least EDGE below the top of the screen on every frame condition is true. A tooltip taller than the screen then starts at the top, title first, and runs off the bottom; scrollBy(int, int) with a negative y brings up the rest, as far as its last line. Several mods may register; any one returning true clamps. Call from client init.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze

    • fitX

      @Internal public static int fitX(int x, int width, int screenWidth)
      Where a tooltip's text starts so its background stays EDGE inside both sides of the screen. Vanilla flips a wide tooltip to the cursor's left but lets one just under the screen's width hang off the right; this pulls it in.     • avoidCoverWhen

      public static void avoidCoverWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Places every tooltip on the side of the cursor where it covers less, on every frame condition is true. MenuKit tries both sides at vanilla's offsets, wrapping text lines to the room up to that screen edge (vanilla's splitter; the first line stays the title, so clampWhen(BooleanSupplier) and scrollBy(int, int) work as before). A side is ruled out only when the tooltip cannot wrap to fit it: its room is narrower than the longest word of any line, an image (a bundle's grid), or MIN_WRAP_WIDTH. Of the sides left, the one whose frame overlaps fewer pixels of what is on the screen wins, however narrow: a container screen's frame (with an open recipe book or creative tab row), every shown MenuKit panel, and the screen's widgets. A tie goes to vanilla's side (right, unless the tooltip does not fit there whole); neither side left places it as vanilla does, and so does a tooltip vanilla anchors to a widget for the keyboard. The height is placed as vanilla does. Several mods may register; any one returning true switches it on. Call from client init.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze

    • scrollBy

      public static void scrollBy(int dx, int dy)
      Moves the tooltip on screen now by dx, dy GUI pixels (positive y moves it down, bringing lines above the screen into view). MenuKit keeps it inside its own extent: a tooltip that fits on screen does not move, and one taller or wider than the screen moves only until its far edge is in view. While a tooltip is scrolled vertically with its top above the screen, its first line (the title) stays pinned at the top edge and the rest scrolls under it. The offset resets by itself when the tooltip changes or goes away.

    • clampScroll

      @Internal public static int clampScroll(int origin, int size, int screen, int offset)
      One axis of a scroll. Vanilla put a tooltip of size at origin on a screen screen long; returns offset clamped so the tooltip moves at most until its far edge sits EDGE inside the screen, and back no further than until its near edge does (or vanilla's spot, if that is further). A tooltip that fits gets 0; one that runs off an end can only scroll toward the hidden part.

    • contentKey

      @Internal public static int contentKey(net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, List<net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.tooltip.ClientTooltipComponent> lines)
      A hash of what a tooltip says, line by line, so "the hovered stack changed" reads as "the text changed" for any tooltip, item or not. Text lines hash their characters; other lines (a bundle's item grid) their kind and size. A 32-bit hash: a collision between two consecutive tooltips would keep the old scroll for one hover. Compare the strings if that ever shows.

    • queue

      public static void queue(net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, net.minecraft.network.chat.Component text, int mouseX, int mouseY, int maxWidthPx)
      Queues a hover tooltip with its own maximum width instead of the default. Pass 0 (or any non-positive value) for no wrapping: one line, as vanilla draws it.

      Wrapping uses Font.split, the splitter in-panel text uses. It breaks at spaces and splits a word only as a last resort, so one very long word can still run past the budget, as in vanilla.

      Parameters:
      graphics - the active GuiGraphicsExtractor
      text - the tooltip text
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      maxWidthPx - the wrap budget in pixels, or <= 0 to not wrap
